<thought>From the spectrum, the M+2 peak is about one‑third the intensity of the monoisotopic peak (≈33 % of M), which matches the characteristic 3:1 isotope pattern of chlorine (³⁵Cl/³⁷Cl). The relatively large M+1 peak (≈16 % of M) is consistent with the cumulative contribution of many ¹³C atoms, indicating the presence of carbon. No 1:1 M+2 pattern (bromine) or the much smaller M+2 contribution of sulfur is observed. Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
